nodes.description: Mouse expressing the limb-girdle P104L caveolin-3 mutant, which loses sarcolemmal caveolin-3 and develops muscular atrophy with raised myostatin pathway activity. It models caveolin-3 deficiency, not the MPDT allele or its hand and foot distribution.

Caveolin-3 carrying the arginine-to-glutamine substitution is mostly retained in the Golgi complex, forms oligomers much larger than wild-type caveolin-3, and is excluded from caveolae-enriched membranes. Whether this allele acts by haploinsufficiency or dominant-negatively is unsettled: co-expression with wild-type caveolin-3 did not show a dominant-negative effect on caveolin-3 itself in one study, whereas another found that it mislocalizes the repair proteins MG53 and dysferlin in a dominant-negative fashion.

nodes.description: Caveolae act as a membrane reservoir that flattens to buffer tension. In patient myotubes with CAV3 variants including R26Q, loss of caveolae leaves the membrane unable to buffer mechanical stress, and IL6/STAT3 signaling becomes constitutively hyperactivated. In zebrafish, a dystrophy-associated caveolin-3 mutant causes sarcolemmal damage only under vigorous muscle activity.

evidence.snippet: This results in impaired regulation of the IL6/STAT3 signaling pathway leading to its constitutive hyperactivation and increased expression of muscle genes.

nodes.description: Preclinical only. In P104L caveolin-3 transgenic mice, crossing in the myostatin prodomain or giving a soluble type II myostatin receptor intraperitoneally reduced muscular atrophy and lowered phosphorylated Smad2 and p21. It has not been tested in patients with MPDT or any other caveolinopathy. No NCIT clinical-action or agent term specific to myostatin inhibition was found (OLS NCIT search for "myostatin inhibitor" and "myostatin propeptide" returned no matching term), so treatment_term and therapeutic_agent are omitted.

nodes.description: Caveolin-3 is greatly reduced at the sarcolemma of patient muscle and caveolae are lost. Caveolin-3 protein deficiency is a sensitive and specific biopsy marker of primary caveolinopathy and is the defining histological finding in MPDT. With caveolin-3 absent from the membrane, its role as a scaffolding protein that organises signalling partners at the sarcolemma is lost as well.

How this contributes to the distal weakness or to muscle hyperexcitability in MPDT has not been shown.
